name: Can One Contractor Handle Multiple Exterior Projects?

mainEntity.name: Can one contractor handle paving, fencing, retaining walls, and driveway work on the same property?
mainEntity.text: Can one contractor handle paving, fencing, retaining walls, and driveway work on the same property?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single contractor can handle multiple exterior improvements if they have the skills and crews to do each scope correctly. That can be efficient for projects that share grading, drainage, access, or demolition work. However, paving, fences, retaining walls, and driveway work each have different technical requirements, so it matters whether the contractor self-performs the work or subcontracts parts of it. In Los Angeles County, coordination is especially important when one project affects another, such as a retaining wall changing drainage or a driveway needing to tie into new hardscape. Ask for a written scope that identifies each trade, timeline, material specifications, and who is responsible for cleanup and inspections. Clear coordination is more important than having the fewest vendors.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but only if the contractor has the right experience, equipment, and licensing for each type of work involved. Some companies can coordinate multiple exterior scopes well, while others are stronger in one specialty and subcontract the rest. The key is whether the proposal clearly states who performs each part and how quality will be managed.
